citations.title: Flavio Cattaneo

sentences.text: Flavio Cattaneo, born in Rho, Italy, in 1963, is a graduate in architecture from the Milan Polytechnic.

He was deputy chairman of AEM Milano (now A2A) from 1998 to 2001, chairman and CEO of Fiera Milano from 1999 to 2003, general manager of RAI from 2003 to 2005, and CEO of Terna from 2005 to 2014, also chairing Brazilian grid operator Terna Participacoes from 2007 to 2011.

sentences.quote:
Between 2017 and 2018 and from 2014 to 2016 he was CEO of NTV-Italo .
From 2016 to 2017 he was CEO of Telecom Italia.
sentences.text: He was CEO of Telecom Italia between 2016 and 2017 and CEO of NTV-Italo in 2014-2016 and 2017-2018.
He has been CEO and general manager of Enel since 12 May 2023, chairman of Enel Iberia and vice chairman of Endesa, and sits on the board of Assicurazioni Generali.
The Enel board appointed by the May 2026 shareholders meeting confirmed him in both roles.

sentences.quote: The Board of Directors of Enel S.p.A. (Enel or the Company), appointed by the Shareholders Meeting on May 12 th, 2026, met today for the first time in Rome and was chaired by Paolo Scaroni.
sentences.text: Enel's board, elected by the shareholders' meeting of May 12, 2026, confirmed Flavio Cattaneo as Chief Executive Officer and General Manager at its first meeting in Rome, chaired by Paolo Scaroni, leaving the existing division of powers unchanged, with the CEO granted all management powers not reserved by law, the bylaws or the board; new directors include Alessandro Monteduro, on the board since May 2026.

sentences.text: Enel states that in 2023-2025 it met the targets announced to the market, completing the disposal plan announced in 2022, reducing net financial debt and distributing about 15 billion euros through dividends and a share buy-back programme, with a 1 billion euro efficiency plan executed ahead of schedule.

sentences.quote: The state-controlled group will invest about 53 billion euros ($63 billion) in the 2026-2028 period, half of which will be dedicated to power grids and roughly 38% to renewables
sentences.text: Capital allocation has tilted toward regulated grids and renewables: the 2026-2028 plan raises investment to about 53 billion euros, half for grids and roughly 38% for renewables, and is expected to lift net financial debt to around three times core earnings.
Buy-backs proceed under a May 2025 shareholder authorisation of up to 3.5 billion euros, with tranches approved by the board.

sentences.quote: Thanks to the clear visibility on Group results and the execution of our share buy-back program, we expect to further increase shareholder remuneration, with an EPS that will increase to between 0.80 and 0.82 euros in 2028
sentences.text: Shareholder remuneration rises with ordinary EPS guided to 0.80-0.82 euros in 2028, supported by the share buy-back programme.
FY2025 ordinary EBITDA was 22.9 billion euros with net debt of 57.2 billion and net debt/EBITDA of 2.5x, with leverage rising to about 3.0x over the plan, still below the sector average.

thesis_pillars.text: Enel's 2026-2028 plan commits around 53 billion euros of gross investments, about 10 billion more than the previous plan, concentrated in the most dynamic geographies. Over 26 billion euros goes to grids, roughly 55% of it in Italy, and over 26 billion to the integrated business, including about 20 billion in renewables to add some 15 GW of capacity. The plan assumes strong electricity demand growth driven by data centres, artificial intelligence, robotics and automation, plus transport electrification and industrial recovery. Shareholder remuneration rises with ordinary EPS guided to 0.80-0.82 euros in 2028, supported by the share buy-back programme.
